sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Hold — unresolved. IC Electricals has a real railway-electronics and electrification business, but recent profit growth is not supported by dependable cash conversion. Material annual-report PAT/cash-flow discrepancies and unverified post-IPO funding prevent an investable return or price conclusion. BQS, Growth Quality Score (GQS) and IAS are NS; exclude financial rankings. This is a funding-sensitive operating-growth/special-situation candidate, not an established compounder. The official 19 October 2026 close of ₹103.05 implies ₹188.19 crore equity value. Revenue reached ₹143.04 crore in FY26, yet FY24–26 cumulative CFO was −₹22.22 crore. The decisive positive is growing output and customer access; the decisive risk is the cash needed to turn booked contracts into collections. A lower price alone cannot resolve a ₹5.764 crore reporting bridge or establish current liquidity. An auditor-backed reconciliation, current bank/use-of-proceeds evidence and attributable reinvestment returns would change the assessment.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: IC Electricals Company Limited; NSE SME ICELCO (SM), ISIN INE0XE501015; incorporated 5 August 2005 and publicly converted 23 September 2024. Information cutoff: 20 October 2026. Market reference: official 19 October final close because 20 October is a market holiday, not a live or executable price. Share count 18,261,600, face value ₹10, lot 1,200. Horizon: 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031; nominal INR pretax equity hurdle 15%, with 12%/18% sensitivities. Illustrative reference position ₹5 lakh is not an allocation recommendation: four lots/4,800 shares cost ₹494,640, while five lots cost ₹618,300. Financial scope is consolidated Indian GAAP (AS), including 60%-owned Safe Coils and the disclosed JV. FY23–26 use IPO-restated accounts; FY21–22 use separately labelled statutory figures. No comparable H1 FY27 cash-flow/TTM set was retrieved by cutoff. G1 Conditional, G2 Hold, G3 Hold, G4 Conditional. Confidence is High on exact identity and historical exchange observations, Medium on recorded sales/output and disclosed historical cash weakness, Low on normalized earnings, incremental economics and current funding. No failure label is inferred from missing information.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS = .20 GOV + .20 MOAT + .12 REV + .10 DUR + .12 CAP + .10 CASH + .08 BAL + .08 EXEC. Growth Quality GQS = .40 REV + .20 DUR + .15 EARN + .15 CAP + .10 CASH. IAS = .25 final BQS + .35 R + .20 D + .10 P + .10 L. Primitive scores: GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 5, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 3, BAL NS, EXEC 5, EARN NS, R NS, D 3, P NS and L 7. Exact Decimal BQS known contribution 3.90, coverage 80%, missing-factor bounds 4.10–5.90; final NS. GQS known 3.50, coverage 70%, raw bounds 3.80–6.50; persistent CASH 3 caps the bounds at 3.80–5.00 but never converts NS into a point. IAS known 1.30, coverage 30%, generic bounds 2.00–8.30; propagating BQS bounds narrows them to 2.7750–7.2750, still not an investment score. G2 prohibits financial ranking. A ±1 judgment change in an observed factor changes only its known weighted contribution and bounds, not the missing final result. Each factor below has facts, counterevidence and traceable evidence IDs.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company designs and manufactures railway electrical/electronic equipment and rotating machinery and executes railway electrification contracts, including 25 kV AC systems. Three Haridwar units support a mixed product portfolio; Safe Coils contributes manufacturing/export operations. FY26 consolidated revenue separates into manufactured-goods sales of ₹84.1111 crore (58.8%) and contracts of ₹58.9304 crore (41.2%). Manufacturing earns on delivered products; EPC economics depend on work completion, certification, billing, retention and collection. This distinction matters because unbilled work is not cash and order announcements are not revenue. Government customers accounted for 81.50% of standalone sales; use that scope explicitly. Exports declined to ₹5.0936 crore, despite new subsidiary announcements. Raw-material inventory, supplier advances, railway security deposits and execution guarantees absorb substantially more capital than net plant assets. The economic bottleneck is not just factory capacity: funded certified throughput and timely collections are equally important.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Railway vendor qualification, product engineering and a record of installed supply create entry friction and access, but the evidence does not establish monopoly economics. Tender/L1 pricing, customer approvals and delivery performance remain contestable. The largest customer share fell to 16.09% and top-ten share to 50.38%, useful diversification but still meaningful concentration. Top-ten suppliers supply 52.59%; long-term supply security is not assumed. Hind Rectifiers is the closest qualitative comparator for railway power conversion and components. HBL Engineering offers a larger technology/qualification benchmark but also batteries/defence; Kernex is an adjacent embedded train-safety comparator. Neither provides a clean ICEL peer multiple or proof that ICEL has Kavach certification. A moat upgrade would require pricing/margin resilience through tenders, retention on repeat products, qualified competitive set and cash returns above capital costs, not just a prestigious customer name. MOAT 5 reflects useful but contestable positioning.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Six annual consolidated observations are available: FY21 ₹94.4584 crore, FY22 ₹97.1469, FY23 ₹97.6935, FY24 ₹99.2492, FY25 ₹121.8859 and FY26 ₹143.0415. The preferred five-year CAGR is 8.6536%; the restated three-year CAGR is 13.5530%. Exact annual additions and YoY rates are embedded in financial_history and shown below. FY21–22 statutory figures are not falsely described as IPO-restated; the older cash/capital bridge is incomplete. The same broad subsidiary/JV business is present, but acquired/organic and price/mix decompositions are not independently established, so this is reported consolidated growth. REV anchor 4 for five-year 5%–10% growth receives one, and only one, trajectory point for two full years of 22.81% and 17.36% growth. Manufacturing pieces rose 25.99% in FY25 and 13.95% in FY26; value/mix and EPC timing also matter. Export revenue fell from ₹9.7403 crore in FY24 to ₹5.0936 crore in FY26, countering a simple secular-export narrative. No ten-year CAGR or seasonal TTM is invented.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Reported production used 48.64% of aggregate 30,384-piece capacity in FY26, versus 33.88% in FY24 and 42.69% in FY25. That creates possible internal room, not proof of low capital intensity: pieces are heterogeneous and execution needs inventories, security deposits and receivable finance. The bottom-up base scenario moves utilization from 53% in FY27 to 80% in FY32, increases weighted realization 2.5% annually and contract revenue 10%; bear and bull paths are explicit in the model. These are analyst assumptions, not management guidance. Base operating NWC/revenue improves from approximately 83.6% historically toward 75%, a meaningful collection/inventory assumption. FY26 reconciled operating invested capital is ₹143.5085 crore, of which ₹20.7691 crore is restricted operating deposits; the funding-side bridge differs by only ₹0.0001 crore rounding. Three-year book incremental NOPAT rose ₹13.6632 crore on ₹73.1348 crore added book capital, an 18.68% diagnostic against assumed nominal 14%–18% cost-of-capital range. It cannot attribute profit recovery to new capital rather than old-capacity utilization or recognition timing. Five-year comparable IC and mature-project returns remain ND, so CAP is NS. Poor cumulative cash realization caps GQS at 5, and missing EARN/CAP leave it NS.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The record supports neither a clean-governance premium nor an unsupported accusation. Related-party procurement increased substantially; Safe System is simultaneously supplier, customer and landlord. FY26 director remuneration of ₹0.684 crore is disclosed, while operating cash remained negative. Company arm’s-length explanations are preserved, but independently reconciled commercial balances and settlement evidence would improve confidence. The original JV agreement, subsequent 1.5%-of-contract-value arrangement for EMC, 49%/99.9% labels and management-certified unaudited accounts require an explicit legal-to-economic-to-consolidation bridge. The prospectus declares no outstanding convertibles and no promoter pledge at its date; promoter control is projected at 60.94% post IPO. October changes are not assumed known. Manufacturing volumes rose, but an older railway APU contract had performance disputes and cancellation; a partly favorable award/payment direction is counterevidence, not a collected cash asset. Transport and other complaints remain contested, not findings of wrongdoing. The dated promises-versus-delivery register below separates realized output from merely announced orders and projected proceeds use. G1 remains Conditional and EXEC 5.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The complete financial history, capital bridge and alternative statutory figures are retained, not compressed into a headline P/E. FY26 operating EBITDA calculated as PBT + all finance cost + depreciation − other income is ₹27.0169 crore; issuer KPI ₹25.6894 crore uses interest only and excludes ₹1.3275 crore other finance charges. This definitional difference is not silently called an arithmetic error. FY26 pre-working-capital operating cash ₹27.4557 crore falls to CFO −₹11.0955 after receivables −₹7.7850, inventory −₹12.1124, other receivables −₹13.2117, other payables −₹5.0836, trade-payable funding +₹2.5453 and taxes −₹2.9037, within rounding. Capex ₹1.0483 crore affects investing cash, not the CFO explanation. FY24–26 CFO/PAT is −0.7899×; FCF proxy totals −₹24.0993 crore before financing interest. Billed receivables over six months improved to ₹4.2110 crore from ₹6.3029; unbilled contract work nevertheless grew to ₹21.1136 crore. Inventory obsolescence and certification-to-collection aging need verification. Compatible COGS/credit-purchase denominators are not established for mixed manufacturing/EPC, so no spurious inventory-day or CCC calculation is presented; rating-agency standalone cycle numbers stay separately labelled.

Material G2 exception: annual-report FY25 PBT ₹6.7588 minus taxes ₹3.3801 gives ₹3.3787, not printed group PAT ₹9.1427; gap ₹5.7640 crore. Its FY26 closing cash flow −₹5.3646 versus balance-sheet +₹0.3994 produces the same gap, as do FY25 −₹5.2270 and +₹0.5370. The scanned originals and issuer duplicate were checked. The annual cash-flow year headings are also inconsistent with the values. A possible duplicate expense presentation is an analyst explanation only; no complete issuer/auditor correction was found. The prospectus tax bridge explains part of FY26 PAT differences but not this complete gap. A later 36-page notice/directors filing is not a corrected full set. Unmodified audit is relevant counterevidence but does not override arithmetic.

Debt ₹75.4245 crore includes ₹21.1172 crore combined related/other demand loans and ₹43.4182 crore cash credit. ₹7.6282 crore margin FDs and other operating security deposits are not unrestricted cash. March statement cash ₹0.3994 comprises ₹0.3834 cash on hand and only ₹0.0160 current bank balance. IPO incremental after-March proceeds are gross less remaining fees, not net proceeds minus prepaid fees again. Demand rollover, facility headroom and current use remain unverified. Opening tax payable and employee provisions, minority claims and contingent exposure are treated once in the model; operational property gets no double-counted standalone value. No actual default or fraud is concluded.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹103.05 and 18,261,600 current shares, equity value is ₹188.1858 crore. Restated FY26 owner PAT yields 13.3690× P/E and ₹7.7081 EPS on the post-IPO denominator; using old reported ₹10.49 EPS would mismatch share bases. Annual-report PAT instead implies 13.1474×, but neither is certified normalized earnings. A mixed-date March-debt EV/EBITDA diagnostic is 9.7561×; current EV and P/B remain null because October cash, deployment, liabilities and equity are unknown. A DCF is not forced onto unreliable working-capital timing. The primary method is explicit annual cash/funding and exit EV-to-equity reconciliation, with reverse P/E expectations as a cross-check.

All ordinary returns and entry prices are null. All conditional non-rescue returns are also null because historical-to-entry reserve gaps are not silently funded by later IPO cash. Separate rescue scenarios assume 25%-discount equity at ₹77.2875, 5% issue fees and actual new shares; no legal or market availability is claimed. Base rescue raises gross ₹6.4636 crore, nets ₹6.1404, expands the share count 4.5796% and dilutes original holders 4.3790%. It generates a counterfactual 12.1436% annual return, below the 15% hurdle; bear and bull are −14.7192% and 26.6429%. The base rescue 12%/15%/18% hurdle values of ₹103.71/₹90.87/₹79.89 are conditional algebra, not authorized ordinary entry prices or a buy range. The October 2031 endpoint uses 202/366 of FY32; no later cash breach controls the horizon. Terminal operating cash is retained, signed cash deficits are not erased, and debt/employee/NCI claims are deducted once. Full 3×3 margin/multiple models and eight linked funding stresses are embedded; downside dilution rises materially when cash assumptions weaken.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest bear case is not merely that railway demand slows. It is that certified-but-uncollected work, inventory and deposits rise while tender margins weaken, bank limits remain tight and demand lenders require repayment. Equity can then be issued at an unfavorable price before reported earnings become cash, permanently reducing per-share participation even if the operating business survives. Annual reporting errors could be corrected without cash loss, but they currently prevent reliable assessment of that risk. The model’s linked stress combines 14% EBITDA margin, 45 extra collection days and restricted operating deposits at 18% of revenue: required gross rescue ₹34.3039 crore, original-holder dilution 19.5527% and counterfactual return −1.2742% annually. It is an assumption test, not a forecast probability or actual funding offer. A 60-day collection stress alone raises gross rescue to ₹14.0653 crore. Conversely, documented post-IPO liquidity, faster certification and actual bank collections could materially improve the bridge. D 3 reflects weak demonstrated protection; an asset-rich balance sheet with tied-up inventory/contract claims is not cash-equivalent downside insurance.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Neither 5× nor 10× is supported by the present evidence. Over five years they require 37.97% and 58.49% annualized share-price growth. At a deliberately lower 10× terminal P/E, no further dilution and a 10% owner margin, a fivefold price needs approximately ₹94.09 crore owner PAT and ₹940.93 crore revenue; tenfold needs ₹188.19 crore PAT and ₹1,881.86 crore revenue. A still lower 8× multiple increases each requirement by 25%, and new shares increase required aggregate earnings proportionately. These are expectation equations, not targets. The current heterogeneous manufacturing capacity is roughly twice FY26 production, not a demonstrated sevenfold or thirteenfold revenue platform; EPC expansion would demand additional working capital, guarantees and execution capability. No validated market share, finance plan or project-level returns support that path. Classification: speculative / unsupported, without a numerical success probability.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Review only disclosed evidence, not price momentum. The ten checkpoints below specify the necessary source, historical baseline and adverse/falsifying development: corrected audited financial statements; current proceeds/bank funding; operating conversion; unbilled certification/collection; inventory aging; debt/ratings; related-party settlements; order delivery and margins; minority/dilution claims; and actual lot-level market access. A favorable order press release alone does not clear any gate. G2 clears only after an authoritative same-scope numerical reconciliation; G3 clears only with dated available funding and linked cash stress that stays above required operating reserves. No automatic future monitoring is represented as already scheduled, and no trade is recommended while these conditions remain unresolved.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved. IC Electricals has a real railway-electronics and electrification business, but recent profit growth is not supported by dependable cash conversion. Material annual-report PAT/cash-flow discrepancies and unverified post-IPO funding prevent an investable return or price conclusion. BQS, Growth Quality Score (GQS) and IAS are NS; exclude financial rankings. This is a funding-sensitive operating-growth/special-situation candidate, not an established compounder. The appropriate action category is research watch / avoid a new evidence-based commitment until the two holds are resolved, not a statement to sell an existing position whose suitability is unknown. All three rankings are disabled. Compounder criteria are not met: incremental return attribution is missing, cash conversion is persistently poor and financial reliability/funding are unresolved. Price dependence matters only after those questions: even the expressly financed base case earns less than the 15% hurdle at the reference price. Recompute using current verified capital and a reconciled profit/cash series before using an entry range, and do not substitute rescue algebra for an ordinary valuation.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary issuer prospectus, statutory annual reports, exchange filings, independent credit-rating rationales and official NSE daily/master data support the analysis. Each material claim has a source ID, locator, date, qualification and decision impact; the register includes original URLs and byte hashes. Original scans, HTML, shareholder registers and OCR are deliberately not in the analytical backups. Safe financial and security-specific extracts permit exact recalculation, but offline reproduction does not reauthenticate original documents or make analyst assumptions true. Peer product pages with unverified publication dates are qualitative context only and do not establish a post-cutoff event. Main open questions: the ₹5.7640 crore annual-statement bridge; corrected fiscal labels; current unrestricted proceeds and available lender limits; legal/economic JV share; group RPT cash settlement; certified unbilled collections; inventory obsolescence; project-level return attribution; and October diluted/pledged capital. Scenario utilization, realizations, contract growth, margins, 2%/4% cash reserve, tax rate 25.5%, recapitalization fees and exit multiples are explicit assumptions. Source limitations affect gate/score outcomes instead of being hidden in a generic disclaimer.

evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Largest/top-ten customer dependence improved versus 30.80%/63.15% prior comparison; government concentration remains. Standalone government percentage is not substituted for consolidated exposure.

evidence.claim: FY26 export revenue 5.0936 crore versus 5.7695 in FY25 and 9.7403 in FY24. July announcement cites a US$510,000 order and US$1.8 million export backlog at 60%-owned Safe Coils; September adds approximately 6 crore rail and 1 crore export orders.
evidence.locator: Prospectus revenue geographical note; dated announcements
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Order announcement is not shipment, profit or cash; 100% subsidiary revenue is consolidated but minority economics must be recognized.

evidence.claim: FY24–26 restated consolidated CFO sums to −22.2243 crore while group PAT totals 28.1365 crore; ratio −0.789874×. Reported capex is only 1.8750 crore across those years.
evidence.locator: PDF352 / F39 and financial history
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Interest is classified in financing cash flow. CFO weakness is working capital/tax, not capex. This ratio uses group PAT to match consolidated CFO.
evidence.decision_impact: CASH 3; persistent poor conversion caps GQS at 5 without filling missing factors.

evidence.claim: FY26 inventory 97.7090 crore, unbilled contract assets 21.1136 crore, billed receivables 35.4558 crore and operating invested capital 143.5085 crore.
evidence.locator: PDF350 and financial notes F46–F68
evidence.status: Verified source fact and analyst bridge
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Restricted deposits 20.7691 crore are operating capital, not available cash; unbilled increased from 8.3648 crore. Management describes completed work awaiting certification/invoice, which is not itself proof of improper recognition.

evidence.claim: The full FY26 annual report prints FY25 PBT 6.7588 crore, tax 3.3801 crore and group PAT 9.1427 crore: an arithmetic discrepancy of 5.7640 crore.
evidence.locator: S3 PDF81 P&L versus S1 PDF351 and restatement notes PDF380
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Scanned statement visually inspected. A likely expense-presentation duplication is an analyst hypothesis, not an issuer correction. The unmodified audit and separate tax restatements do not reconcile the complete discrepancy.
evidence.decision_impact: G2 Hold; financial quality rankings excluded.

evidence.claim: Annual-report FY26 cash-flow closing balance −5.3646 crore differs from its balance-sheet cash +0.3994 crore by 5.7640 crore. FY25 corresponding balances −5.2270 and +0.5370 have the same gap.
evidence.locator: S3 PDF80–82; issuer duplicate PDF81; later directors filing p21
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Annual cash-flow headings say FY25/FY24 although left-column flows align with FY26. September 29 file is not a complete corrected set; issuer-hosted duplicate retains the anomaly. No fraud inferred.
evidence.decision_impact: G2 Hold; no certified normalized PAT/EARN score.

evidence.claim: FY26 restated owner PAT 14.0763 crore differs from annual-report 14.3135 crore; part of the difference is identified tax restatement, while FY25 PAT/cash discrepancies remain unresolved.
evidence.locator: Restatement note PDF380; annual PDF81
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Normal standalone/consolidated differences are not called errors; this is a same-scope arithmetic and comparative bridge exception. EBITDA using all finance costs is 27.0169 crore; issuer interest-only KPI 25.6894 excludes 1.3275 crore loan-processing/other finance charges.

evidence.claim: March 2026 gross borrowings 75.4245 crore versus available statement cash 0.3994 crore; cash includes only 0.0160 crore current bank balance and 0.3834 crore cash on hand.
evidence.locator: Financial notes F46–F68; financial-indebtedness chapter
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Current post-IPO bank balances, available undrawn limits and deployment are not verified. NBFC facilities carry 14%–18.75% stated rates. PNB limit/outstanding discrepancy needs reconciliation, not an automatic default allegation.
evidence.decision_impact: G3 Hold and BAL NS, rather than invented liquidity or a verified default.

evidence.claim: CARE 5 March 2026 rates facilities CARE BB+/Stable and A4+ and calls liquidity stretched, with 97% fund-based utilization and 79% non-fund utilization over twelve months to December 2025. Infomerics 2 March 2026 reaffirms BB+/Stable and A4+.
evidence.locator: Rating rationales, liquidity paragraphs
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: CARE uses standalone FY25 and its own working-capital definitions: 250-day cycle, 273 inventory days, 125 collection days. They are not the same denominators as the consolidated model. No actual payment default verified.
evidence.decision_impact: Independent corroboration of funding sensitivity, not current sanctioned availability.

evidence.claim: Fresh IPO 4,839,600 shares at 99 rupees gives gross 47.91204 crore. Estimated expenses 7.1868 include 1.2619 prepaid by March, leaving incremental post-March cash 41.98714 if settled. WC object 33.6 and GCP 7.1252 crore.
evidence.locator: PDF110 and130–138, objects and capital structure
evidence.status: Verified issue terms; actual deployment ND
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Main objects reconcile 40.7252 net proceeds; later schedule prints GCP 7.1868, a 0.0616 crore discrepancy. Current unspent funds and final issue costs unavailable; proceeds are not counted twice or called current surplus cash.
evidence.decision_impact: No ordinary funded IRR or entry range until current bridge verified.

evidence.claim: Related demand loans 15.4123 crore and other demand loans 5.7049 crore sit alongside cash credit 43.4182 crore, current term maturities 8.5817 and other long-term debt 2.3073 crore.
evidence.locator: Financial debt notes and related-party schedule
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Some related loans described as interest free, while SHBD interest of 0.3506 crore is separately reported; no blanket free-funding assumption. Demand/CC rollover remains unverified.

evidence.claim: Contingent claims 11.5312 crore and guarantees/LC 37.3437 crore. LC/BG-backed trade payables of 17.9423 crore are a subset, not a second certain debt. Employee provisions 1.1755 and income-tax payable 4.9991 crore are included separately once.
evidence.locator: Contingencies, payables, tax and employee notes
evidence.status: Verified source fact and model treatment
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Claims are disputed; stress assumes incremental net crystallization only, not total contingent face value plus underlying obligations.

evidence.claim: Related purchases from Safe Insulation rose to 7.6554 crore from 0.4838; Safe System purchases 1.0192, sales 8.0563 and rent 0.336 crore. Director remuneration 0.684 crore.
evidence.locator: RPT note F63–F65 and directors disclosures
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Company describes arrangements as arm’s-length. No substantiated diversion concluded; procurement growth, counterparty balances and cash settlement need independent confirmation.

evidence.claim: JV ownership/economic labels differ: original 49% agreement, subsequent arrangement gives EMC 1.5% contract value while ICEL bears execution, AOC shows 99.9%, and accounts are management certified without separate audit.
evidence.locator: Prospectus JV/control note; annual audit other matter PDF73 and AOC p32
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Company provides a contractual control explanation; a full legal/economic/accounting bridge is still needed. Negative JV net assets and small profit are disclosed, not ignored.
evidence.decision_impact: GOV/EARN confidence constrained; not automatically improper consolidation.

evidence.claim: Commercial disputes include transport-payment complaint and a railway APU performance case. Railway cancelled an old ten-unit order after two deliveries; a partly favorable award and later payment direction support company counterclaims.
evidence.locator: PDF426–446, particularly430–436
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Company disputes the transport claim and says another complaint copy was not received. Court/award developments are not proof of realized cash; allegations are not findings of guilt. Company states no recent debarment/blacklisting.
evidence.decision_impact: G1 Conditional, not Fail; execution history is mixed.

evidence.claim: Prospectus says no outstanding convertible instruments and no promoter/promoter-group pledge as of prospectus date; promoter control is projected at 60.94% post issue.
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Latest October encumbrance/free-float changes not independently verified. The 2:1 bonus is not economic dilution; FY25 private placements and the fresh IPO are.
evidence.decision_impact: Do not assume current fully diluted claims beyond verified issued share base.

evidence.claim: Official 19 October close is 103.05 rupees; one lot costs 123,660. Four lots cost 494,640 and five cost 618,300 against illustrative 500,000 reference.
evidence.locator: Final close and security master; all 60 sessions in safe extract
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: 60/60 sessions observed, no absent row mislabelled zero. Mean/median turnover and whole-lot constraints do not establish executable spread or queue priority.
evidence.decision_impact: L 7 with explicit two-point reduction from continuous-day anchor 9; G4 Conditional.

evidence.claim: Core operating IC of 143.5085 crore reconciles to funding-side 143.5086 within 0.0001 rounding. Three-year book incremental NOPAT/capital proxy is 18.6822%.
evidence.locator: Financial extracts and capital bridge
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Profit recovery/utilization can raise the proxy without new-capital returns. Cohort or commissioned-asset attribution absent; five-year capital/cash restriction bridge incomplete. Nominal capital-cost range 14%–18% is an assumption.
evidence.decision_impact: CAP NS, never a score from current ROCE alone.

evidence.claim: All non-rescue models have pre-entry reserve breaches. Separate base rescue requires gross 6.4636 crore, fees 0.3232, net 6.1404 and 836,301 new shares at assumed 77.2875 rupees.
evidence.locator: Full annual/boundary model rows
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Base share-count expansion 4.5796% differs from holder dilution 4.3790%. Pre-entry recapitalization changes the historical capital structure. Legal, market and funding availability unverified.
evidence.decision_impact: Ordinary and non-rescue conditional IRRs/entry prices remain null.

evidence.claim: Base explicit rescue yields 12.1436% annualized over 19 October 2026–19 October 2031, below 15% hurdle; linked 14% margin/45-day collection/restricted-capital stress requires gross 34.3039 crore and 19.5527% holder dilution.
evidence.locator: Scenario, full sensitivity and linked-stress rows
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: Exit 8× EBITDA and operating-cash reserve are assumptions, not target recommendation. All required cash and creditor/NCI claims are retained once.

evidence.claim: Hind Rectifiers overlaps in railway power electronics; HBL and Kernex illustrate railway qualification/embedded-safety competition but have materially different business mixes.
evidence.locator: Official product pages and HBL FY25 report
evidence.qualification_or_counterevidence: No peer valuation median, market share or common accounting comparability asserted. ICEL is not inferred to possess competitors’ Kavach certifications.

liquidity.restriction_note: Official master SM active row has eligibility 1, normal market status 6 and CallAuctnInd 5; raw codes retained, unsupported code meanings not inferred.
